title: Shortfall: invoice exception workbench
shortDescription: Resolve invoice quantity discrepancies with cited evidence, approvals tied to current records, and durable execution. Shortfall runs on Vultr and tracks a case from a late receipt through an approved supplier credit.
longDescription:
Shortfall helps accounts payable reviewers resolve quantity discrepancies as receiving evidence changes. Manual review requires comparing the invoice, purchase order, and receipts, recalculating late updates, and recording the decision for the next reviewer. Existing accounting systems offer matching controls; Shortfall focuses on completing the exception.

Each case combines cited source fields, calculated amounts, approval against current evidence, assigned tasks, and execution history. The expected benefit is less searching, repeated arithmetic, and handover work. Tracking receipts and credits helps address the risk of approving unreceived quantities, missing a credit, or retaining an outdated hold.

In the synthetic demo, 120 units at $40 produce a $4,800 invoice. With 100 received, the gap is $800. A late receipt adds ten units, reducing it to $400. The server rejects the old approval. A reviewer approves the revised hold, then a verified $400 credit and hold release. The result is $4,400 net with ten purchase order units open.

Vultr hosts the web/API, PostgreSQL, and durable worker. Claude Opus 5.5 extracts fields and source quotes; code validates evidence, calculates money, checks approval revisions, and prevents duplicate execution.

The original 24 document evaluation accepted 9/12 supported inputs, sent three valid CSVs to review, and met all 12 other expected outcomes. After a validator fix, three targeted reruns passed. Four fresh CSV cases then met their expected acceptance or review outcomes. The report keeps these synthetic sets separate.

The internal demo ledger has no bank or ERP connection. Time and cost savings remain unmeasured; a $400 correction is not cash saved. Cases support USD, whole units, and one invoice per supplier/order. The proposed buyer is a distributor's finance manager; $99/workspace/month is a price to test. Next: operator interviews, authenticated roles, and an accounting connector.
